Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 High-entropy engineering is applied to LMFP cathodes, suppressing Jahn-Teller distortion and accelerating charge-transfer kinetics—a strategy not previously demonstrated for this composition. This addresses LMFP's key limitations (sluggish kinetics, Mn dissolution), enabling higher energy density than LiFePO4 while improving rate performance and cycling stability, marking a significant advance toward practical high-energy olivine cathodes for Li-ion batteries.

item.description:

Nano Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in identifying weak Zn–O bonds as the cause of irreversible interlayer Zn migration and voltage hysteresis in oxygen-redox Na-layered cathodes, and proposing a local coordination environment regulation strategy that strengthens Zn–O bonds to suppress migration. This reduces voltage hysteresis from 1.47 to 0.97 V and nearly doubles capacity retention, offering a universal design principle for high-energy sodium-ion batteries.

item.title: Atomic‐Level Topological Defect Reconstruction: Boron‐Induced Lattice Editing of Pitch‐Derived Carbon for High‐Performance Potassium‐Ion Storage
item.description:
بازسازی نقص توپولوژیکی با بور، نیتروژن پیرولیک پنج‌عضوی ناپایدار را به پیکربندی پایدار B–N شش‌عضوی تبدیل کرده و ذخیره‌سازی سریع و پایدار K+ در آند کربنی را بهبود می‌دهد.
Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using electron-deficient boron to selectively convert unstable five-membered pyrrolic-N into stable six-membered B–N configurations, reconstructing defect topology at the atomic level. This repairs π-conjugation while creating polarized B–N domains that optimize K+ affinity without deep trapping, enabling fast kinetics and 3000-cycle stability. It offers a topology-oriented design principle balancing adsorption, transport, and structural stability in carbon anodes.

item.title: Terminal Charge Topology Directs Molecular Adsorption Configuration for Trace‐Level Electrolyte Additives Toward Stable Zinc Anodes

Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in linking terminal charge topology of electrolyte additives to their adsorption configuration and concentration-dependent interfacial regulation. Dianionic FDP enables parallel adsorption, achieving high Zn surface coverage at far lower concentration. This yields 99.92% Coulombic efficiency and stable Zn-MnO₂ cycling over 1000 cycles, clarifying molecular design principles for trace-level additives in aqueous zinc batteries.

item.title: Asymmetric SWCNT/PFSA Bilayer Membranes Enhancing Performance and Mechanical Durability in PEM Fuel Cells
item.description:

Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in an asymmetric bilayer design confining a functionalized SWCNT/PFSA composite layer to one side of a thin PFSA membrane, avoiding a through-plane CNT pathway while exploiting the hydration-stabilizing interface. Its significance is delivering 2.29 W cm⁻² and 95% power retention after 3000 wet/dry cycles with low hydrogen crossover, offering a practical route to durable, high-performance thin membranes.
🏷 PFSA membrane · SWCNT composite · PEM fuel cell · proton transport · hydrogen crossover
